evidence: firmware_acceptance/kit.py:170-314: AcceptanceBroker only materializes/configures/records/adopts pre-existing evidence; its class documentation states it never dispatches MCP itself.

orchestrator_harness/lane_controller.py:1-533 and repository-wide rg for AcceptanceBroker/controller_config/evaluate_call: lane_controller neither imports nor invokes firmware_acceptance; schema-less mcp_servers is only parsed and recorded, not launched or brokered.
firmware_acceptance/README.md:3-5 calls the kit a static test medium and says a future controller alone starts the server and produces the call chain.

orchestrator_harness/tests/test_firmware_acceptance_host.py:37-64 and test_firmware_acceptance_kit.py:16-25 construct every stage, signature, raw result, and exact_reaped value directly before calling admit; no test exercises an executable controller-to-MCP request/response lifecycle.

GENERALIZATION_SPEC_2.md:313 requires each candidate controller to own the MCP process/stdio and broker every physical interaction, rejecting forwarding without the ordered valid artifacts; EXECUTION_READINESS_2.md:101-110 requires only that controller to receive the physical capability and to forward structured O/worker requests after validation.
findings.observed: The candidate contains a static, host-only validator and a generic Codex lane controller, but no C3-HARNESS controller path that receives a structured request, creates/verifies the required proposal-decision-authorization-admission chain, starts the pinned MCP process, forwards an admitted call, records its raw result, and performs exact process/claim cleanup.
findings.expected: C3-HARNESS must be an executable candidate control plane: it alone launches target workers and lane-owned MCP processes, retains the physical endpoint, brokers only admitted requests, and produces lifecycle/evidence records sufficient for C3/C4.
findings.reproduction: Read-only trace: search the candidate for AcceptanceBroker, controller_config, and evaluate_call. Their only production definitions are in firmware_acceptance/kit.py; the only other references are tests and package exports. Trace lane_controller.run: it launches only the Codex child and has no firmware_acceptance import, MCP subprocess creation, structured-request input, forwarding, or MCP cleanup path. The current S2 host tests instead call broker.record repeatedly with synthetic signature/raw-result/exact_reaped fields.
findings.impact: A future F.C3.O cannot submit an assignment to a candidate-owned C3-HARNESS that can perform the mandated physical work. Either C3 is blocked outright, or an operator/O/target worker must add a direct MCP launch/dispatch path outside the candidate, which violates the exclusive-capability and topology requirements and makes physical acceptance non-certifying.
findings.no_fix_consequence: The candidate cannot satisfy its central physical acceptance contract; passing the present synthetic tests would provide no evidence that server ownership, authorization-before-forwarding, timeout/expiry handling, raw-result capture, or exact MCP cleanup works in a real controller lifecycle.
findings.smallest_fix: Add a narrowly scoped firmware acceptance controller entry point integrated with the existing lane-controller ownership model. It should consume only structured broker requests, instantiate AcceptanceBroker, launch/reap the pinned stdio MCP process with its returned controller-only configuration, create/verify the immutable stages and signature/authorization hooks, forward only after admission, capture the real raw result, and retain claims through exact cleanup. Add synthetic subprocess/stdio tests proving this end-to-end boundary and direct-endpoint denial; keep the legacy schema-less route unchanged.
findings.complexity: Moderate: one bounded controller/broker integration plus fake-stdio lifecycle tests; it reuses the existing static policy, evidence, seed, and exact-child cleanup primitives rather than introducing a scheduler or framework.
findings.regression_risk: Moderate but contained: isolate the new behavior behind the C3 firmware controller entry point and retain the existing coding V1 and schema-less legacy loaders unchanged; rerun the mapped controller and cross-route suites.
findings.verification_cost: Moderate: host-only fake pinned MCP subprocess tests for admission, forwarding, expiry/timeout, crash cleanup, and endpoint isolation, followed by the required later C2/C3 evidence gates.
findings.alternatives: Leaving the kit static is not viable because the governing documents require a candidate-owned executable control plane. Giving F.C3.O or target workers the MCP declaration would reduce code now but directly violates the required capability/topology boundary.
findings.cost_benefit: This is the smallest implementation that turns the already-created policy/evidence kit into the required operable harness boundary. Its bounded complexity and test cost are outweighed by preventing an unavoidable C3 block or an uncertifiable direct physical-MCP bypass.
